title: Protocol for analysis of integrin-mediated cell adhesion of lateral plate mesoderm cells isolated from zebrafish embryos
protocol: Set up zebrafish to breed in a separate breeding tank.
Remove the divider separating male and female fish to initiate breeding.
Rinse embryos on a strainer with 0.03% sea salt solution.
Transfer cleaned embryos into a 10-cm petri dish containing E3 medium.
Transfer 17 hpf embryos into a beaker containing E3 medium.
Treat the embryos with Pronase solution.
Observe that chorions start to break open.
Transfer dechorionated embryos into a 10-cm petri dish containing E3 medium.
Initiate breeding by removing the divider separating male and female fish when the light comes on.
Pour water and embryos through a mesh tea strainer to collect the embryos after spawning.
Rinse the collected embryos well with a 0.03% sea salt solution.
Wash the rinsed embryos into a 10-cm petri dish using E3 medium.
Keep the embryos in petri dishes containing E3 medium at a density of less than 30 embryos per dish until 17 hpf at 28°C.
Transfer Tg(fli1a:EGFP)y1 zebrafish embryos to glass beakers at 17 hpf.
Incubate the embryos in Pronase solution at 20-25°C for 5-10 minutes.
Incubate the embryos once per minute and check the chorions under a microscope.
Wash the embryos thoroughly with E3 medium when the chorions start to break open.
Pipette the embryos back and forth in E3 medium using a plastic Pasteur pipette to remove chorions.
Collect dechorionated embryos in a 10-cm petri dish containing E3 medium.
Transfer fifteen embryos into a 2 mL-Eppendorf tube.
Wash the embryos with 1 mL of PBS once.
Incubate the embryos with 500 μL of 1× Liberase solution at 37°C for 1 hour.
Gently mix the embryos every 20 minutes during incubation using a P1000 single channel pipette.
Add 1 mL of Liberase termination solution to terminate the enzymatic reaction.
Dissociate embryonic cells by gentle pipetting using a P1000 pipette.
Filter dissociated cells through a 100-μm cell strainer.
Collect filtered cells in new 2 mL-Eppendorf tubes.
Centrifuge the cells at 1,600 rpm (approximately 250 × g) for 3 minutes at 15–25°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of DPBS.
Pellet the cells suspended in DPBS by centrifugation at 1,600 rpm (approximately 250 × g) for 3 min at 15–25°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of Leibovitz’s L15 culture medium.
Plate 200 μL of the resuspended cells onto a fibronectin-coated glass bottom dish (12-mm diameter).
Incubate the cells at 28°C for 13 h to allow them to adhere to the fibronectin-coated dish.
Gently wash the adherent cells with PBS twice.
Fix the cells with fixative solution for 20 min at 15–25°C.
Permeabilize the cells with permeabilization solution for 30 min at 4°C.
Wash the cells with PBS three times briefly.
Incubate the cells with blocking solution for 90 min at 15–25°C.
Incubate the cells with rabbit anti-GFP antibody (1:300 dilution) and mouse anti-vinculin antibody (1:300 dilution) dissolved in PBS at 4°C for 12–16 h.
Wash the cells with PBS three times for 10 min each.

Label proteins reacting with primary antibodies by incubating the cells with PBS containing Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated goat anti-rabbit IgG antibody (1:1000 dilution) and Alexa Fluor 564-conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG antibody (1:1000 dilution) for 2 h at 15–25°C.
Wash the cells with PBS six times for 10 min each.
Incubate the cells with PBS containing Alexa Fluor 633-conjugated phalloidin (1:1000 dilution) for 2 h at 15–25°C to visualize filamentous actin.
Wash the cells with PBS three times for 10 min each.
Submerge the cells with PBS.
Define a region where GFP-positive LPM cells are present.
Select the GFP-positive LPM cells that are not in contact with the surrounding GFP-negative cells.
Acquire fluorescence image volumes of Alexa Fluor 488 (GFP).
Acquire fluorescence image volumes of Alexa Fluor 546 (vinculin).
Acquire fluorescence image volumes of Alexa Fluor 633 (F-actin).
Open the images using ImageJ software.
Install Bio-Formats in ImageJ to open Olympus OIF files.
Create Z-projections.
Set the scale using an image with a calibration scale if size information is lost.
Draw a straight line that defines a known distance on your calibration image using the “straight line selection” tool.
Fill in the “Known distance” without units.
Define the units of length in the “Unit of Length” field.
Click on “Global” so that this calibration applies to all images that you open in this ImageJ session.
Click “OK”.
Select the GFP-positive cell for analysis.
Draw the outline of the GFP-positive cell by using Freehand selections.
[Edit]→[Clear Outside]
Separate images for each channel.
[Image]→[Color]→[Split Channels]
Select the Alexa Fluor 546 image (vinculin).
Subtract background.
[Process]→[Subtract Background]
Chose the “Sliding Paraboloid” option with the “Rolling ball radius” set to 50 pixels.
Enhance the local contrast of the image.
[Plugin]→[CLAHE]
Set the values as follows; block size = 19, histogram bin = 256, maximum slope = 6.
Minimize the background.
[Process]→[Math]→[Exp]
Adjust brightness and contrast.
[Image]→[Adjust]→[Brightness/Contrast]
Click “Auto” and “Apply”.
Run Log3D (Laplacian of Gaussian) filter.
[Plugin]→[Log3D]
Define the size of the Log3D filter as sigma X = 3 and sigma Y = 3.
Install "Log3D plugin" in ImageJ from the Sage website.
Set the threshold using [Adjust]→[Threshold].
Click “Apply” to apply the threshold settings.
Run analyze particles through [Analyze]→[Analyze Particles].
Set parameters for particle analysis: Size = 0–infinity, Circularity = 0.00–0.99.
Select the “Show: Outlines” option in particle analysis.
Check “Display results” and “Summarize” options.
